description:
## Site
apps/octo_pi_agent/lib/octo_pi/agent.ex L141:

\`\`\`elixir
@spec set_messages(t(), [term()]) :: :ok
def set_messages(pid, msgs) when is_list(msgs), do: GenServer.call(pid, {:set_messages, msgs})
\`\`\`

Unlike prompt/steer/follow_up, this does NOT route through
\`Message.normalize/1\`. Coder.Loop calls it after compaction with
messages reconstructed from the session store — those happen to come
out list-shape today (MessageReader.content_blocks/1 lifts strings
on read), but nothing in the API contract enforces that. Any future
caller passing a binary-content User struct silently breaks the
list-only invariant from opi-5ka.1.

## Change
\`\`\`elixir
@spec set_messages(t(), [Message.t() | String.t()]) :: :ok
def set_messages(pid, msgs) when is_list(msgs),
  do: GenServer.call(pid, {:set_messages, Message.normalize(msgs)})
\`\`\`

## Test
- New test in agent_test.exs (or loop_behavior_test.exs): pass a
  mixed list \`[\"a\", %User{content: \"b\", ...}, %User{content: [%Text{text: \"c\"}], ...}]\`
  to set_messages and assert the resulting state.messages all have
  list-shape content.

## Depends on
opi-5ka.1 (so normalize already lifts).
title: Plug Agent.set_messages/2 normalization gap
